title: Students protest RSS leader's presence and suspensions at Central University of Kerala
seoTitle: Kasaragod student protests over RSS leader

tea.why: Students opposed the presence of an RSS leader at a university seminar and the subsequent suspension of five students.
tea.want: Protesters demand the entry of registered students to events and the revocation of student suspensions.
tea.changed: Oct 9: Police used water cannons to disperse a student march protesting the suspension of five students.

summary: Students at the Central University of Kerala in Kasaragod launched protests on October 6, 2026, opposing the presence of J Nandakumar, an RSS-linked leader, at a Vande Mataram seminar. Organised by groups including the Students' Federation of India (SFI), Kerala Students Union (KSU), and Muslim Students Federation (MSF), the demonstrators also alleged that registered students were barred from the event. Following scuffles, the university suspended five students and police booked 25 student leaders. On October 9, 2026, an SFI-led march protesting these suspensions escalated when police used water cannons to prevent students from breaching barricades. Protesters vowed to continue their agitation.
demands: Allow registered students to attend university events
Oppose the saffronisation of higher education institutions
Revoke the suspension of five students
response: The university suspended five students for two weeks and evicted them from hostels. Police registered a case against 25 student leaders and deployed water cannons and barricades to disperse protesters.

updates.text: Students protested RSS leader J Nandakumar's presence at a university seminar, leading to scuffles with police who blocked them from entering.
The university suspended five students for two weeks and evicted them from hostels, while police registered a case against 25 student leaders.
Police used water cannons to disperse an SFI-led protest march against the student suspensions as demonstrators tried to breach barricades.
